items.rationale: A stranger watching is a small, noticed worry for a hunted man, likely nothing.
A large bounty is on his head and the one person sheltering him is asking what it pays, which puts his life on the line.
His friend gets a week's reprieve, a small relief that leaves the bigger question open.
His closest friend now has lasting protection from the people hunting him.
If Halvorsen comes through this building, the stall and the room where his daughter sleeps are in the way, a worry he notices.
A stray stimpak from the runner she shelters is a token of deference that barely registers.
Her tenant turned down her rival in front of Vance's crew and now pays her, a real affirmation of her hold on the street.
A cell worth more than the two months owed is real money toward the 1,500 she is short for Kessler.
Rogue taking the cell clears the arrears that had his stall, his living and his daughter's home, one month from being taken.
Setting his own fan speed is a trivial bit of extra control.
He can now choose his own jobs from anywhere instead of working through Rogue's line, a lasting change in how free he is.
No sale tonight leaves him short for groceries, an annoyance that does not change his situation.
Rogue let his only way to clear the arrears go unanswered, leaving the stall and home she just threatened to take still at stake.
His one friend's last way of keeping his stall was ignored by Rogue, a real worry Glitch will carry for days.
A client grumbling about one late runner is a minor knock to her record.
A major client has dropped her as someone who cannot deliver, a lasting mark on her record as a fixer.
That verdict spreading to every corp downtown cuts into the standing her hold on the street rests on.
An 800-eddy job means he can send his sister the money she is waiting on.
He must run it entirely her way, a small, noticed limit on his own judgement.
The fixer who runs the street vouched for his skill to her whole bar.
Her word may bring a few more customers to a stall that needs them.
Her standing is affirmed aloud in her bar just as Vance's people are asking, a small, noticed boost.
He can no longer come and go as he chooses, a real limit on his days.
Rogue is watching the street for him and keeping him in, a small added protection.
A free drink is a small pleasure gone from mind within the hour.
The deadly debt she could not cover in three days is gone along with the crew that would have killed her for it.
He loses the say over his own stock and prices, a lasting change in how he runs his stall.
A tenth of the till taken from a stall two months behind makes catching up on rent harder.
The fixer who judges runners named his run the best she has seen this year.
Her conditional promise of a place is a small easing of his worry about being thrown out.
His living and his daughter's home, a month from being lost, are now his outright and safe from rent and from Vance.
He now owns the premises he works from instead of being a tenant in arrears.
